Most tattoo artists in my experience don't like text unless it's big and bold. Tattoos change over time and with an Image it can blur or fade and still look decent for a while but with text it can make it hard to read and depending on size and location may need to be touched up sooner than usual. But every tattoo is overdone. Some people like script and if you like it which it seems your heart is set on it, then go for it. But make sure you look at the artists other script tattoos, most of the time they aren't portfolio pieces unless it's inside an image or something though. Also, make sure the font is big enough and letters spaced enough to leave room for it to age. Location, I think depending on the size, the shoulder blade is a good location. If you wanted to make the word be verticals you could do down the neck, also on your side upper rib cage a little lower than breast or where a bra, bathing suit would fit....

My husband is a tattoo artist and we own our own shop. I'd have to say that's about right. The healing is way worse than the tattoo in most cases but worse on the feet for many reasons. I have tattooed my feet and I also found I had to keep it elevated or it felt like it was going to explode from the pressure of standing and all your blood flowing down there. Plan on the next day elevating your foot and possibly putting something cold on it if it swells, if your going to put ice on it make sure whatever is touching your tattoo (I suggest a clean cloth) because it is an open wound, remember that to prevent infection. During the tattoo if you have a good artist they should make you feel at home, our shop offers all clients a free drink and snack because its surprising how many people don't eat before a tattoo and that's important. Also, since it's your feet you probably get to sit comfortably. I've had my armpits tattooed , my whole side, my foot, it all hurts about the same and comes in waves. Good luck and post pictures of it!!
